findings.title: --flusher-processes defaults to 1, so the PR's one-process-per-shard behavior is not the default
findings.body: The new `--flusher-processes` option defaults to 1, and the factory forwards that value as `max_processes`. `SpanFlusher` then runs `min(max_processes, len(shards))` processes, so with the default every shard in the consumer is flushed by a single process. The PR description says the flusher should spawn a process per redis shard, but that only happens when operators pass a higher value explicitly. Either the default should be unset/None (meaning one process per shard) or the description and help text should say the default is a single process.

findings.title: time.sleep(0.1) is a no-op in this test, so the wait for the flusher is not real
findings.body: `test_basic` monkeypatches `time.sleep` to a no-op at the top of the test, and the added `time.sleep(0.1)` call uses that same patched function. The comment says it gives flusher threads time to process after the drift change, but the call returns immediately. The test then calls `step.join()` and asserts on `messages`, so it can race with the flusher thread and fail intermittently. The wait needs to use a real sleep or a deterministic synchronization point.

findings.title: _create_process_for_shard is never called
findings.body: `_create_process_for_shard` (singular) is added but nothing in the diff or the surrounding code calls it; restarts go through `_create_process_for_shards` in `_ensure_processes_alive`. This is dead code that also has a misleading name next to the plural method.

findings.title: Inconsistent metric tag key between flusher timers ('shard' vs 'shards')
findings.body: The `spans.buffer.flusher.produce` and `segment_size_bytes` metrics use the tag key `shard`, while `spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce` uses `shards`. Dashboards and alerts filtering on one key will silently miss the other timer's data.

findings.title: Hung thread-based flushers are restarted without being stopped
findings.body: In `_ensure_processes_alive`, `process.kill()` is only called for `multiprocessing.Process`. For the `threading.Thread` path (used in tests with `produce_to_pipe`), a hung thread is left running and a second thread for the same shards is started. Both then flush the same buffer. This is limited to the test path, but it means restart behavior differs between modes.

findings.title: join() stops waiting on deadline but does not terminate the remaining processes
findings.body: In `join`, when the deadline passes the loop breaks before reaching the remaining processes, so those processes are never terminated. They are daemons, but the explicit termination step is skipped for them, so shutdown can leave child processes running.

findings.title: Unrelated anti-pattern section added to CLAUDE.md in a span flusher PR
findings.body: The CLAUDE.md change adds a 'hasattr() for unions' example that has nothing to do with the multiprocessed flusher. It also places an extra blank line before the closing code fence. This should be split into its own change or dropped.
